tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List all projects visible to this agent.

tools.name: list_artifacts
tools.description: List artifacts in a project, optionally filtered by type and by owner (the "owner" attribute: a person, team or supplier).

owner.description: Optional owner filter: only artifacts whose owner attribute equals this

tools.name: get_artifact
tools.description: Get a single artifact by ID, including its body. Accepts a stable ref (e.g. "REQ-12") instead of a UUID when project_id is also given.

id.description: Artifact ID (UUID), or a stable ref like REQ-12 (requires project_id)

project_id.description: Project ID; required only when id is a stable ref

tools.name: get_project_map
tools.description: The project's AI map: every artifact as one outline line — stable ref, title, status, hierarchy, and inline link annotations, no bodies. Roughly 10x fewer tokens than list_artifacts; use it to orient, then pull bodies for specific artifacts with get_artifact or get_context. Pass baseline_id for the map as of a baseline/release.

baseline_id.description: Optional baseline ID to render the map from that snapshot

tools.name: get_context
tools.description: One-call context bundle for an artifact: full body, ancestor path, children, and every linked artifact with a short excerpt — addressed by stable ref (REQ-12) or UUID. Replaces a get_artifact + list_links_for_artifact + N more get_artifact round trip.

id.description: Artifact stable ref (e.g. REQ-12) or UUID

tools.name: get_project_tree
tools.description: Get the project's artifact tree: id, type, title, parent_id, sort_order per artifact (no bodies).

tools.name: search_artifacts
tools.description: Case-insensitive substring search over artifact refs, titles and bodies in a project. A query that is a ref ("REQ-30", case-insensitive) returns that artifact first.

query.description: Substring to search for, or a ref such as REQ-30

tools.name: create_artifact
tools.description: Create an artifact. A 202 response means the change was diverted to a proposal pending human review. In proposal mode you may pass a `ref`: a temporary token you choose (e.g. "t1") that names this not-yet-created artifact so a create_link in the SAME run can point at it via from_id/to_id. The token resolves to the real artifact id when the artifact proposal is approved.

ref.description: Optional temporary reference token (proposal mode only) to name this artifact for a sibling create_link in the same run

tools.name: update_artifact
tools.description: Update an artifact. Omitted optional fields are left unchanged. A 202 response means the change was diverted to a proposal pending human review.

attributes.description: Optional attributes object (omit to keep current)

body.description: Optional markdown body (omit to keep current; pass "" to clear)

parent_id.description: Optional new parent artifact ID (omit to keep current; pass "" to move to the top level)

type.description: Optional artifact type (omit to keep current)

tools.name: create_link
tools.description: Create a typed link between two artifacts. In proposal mode from_id and/or to_id may be a temporary ref token that a create_artifact in the SAME run assigned via its `ref` argument, letting you link to an artifact whose own proposal is not yet approved; the token resolves to the real id when both proposals are approved (the artifact one first). A 202 response means the link was diverted to a proposal pending human review.

from_id.description: Source artifact ID, or a ref token from a create_artifact in this run

to_id.description: Target artifact ID, or a ref token from a create_artifact in this run

tools.name: delete_link
tools.description: Delete a link by ID.

tools.name: confirm_link
tools.description: Clear the suspect flag on one link, vouching that the trace still holds after an artifact at one of its ends changed. Re-read both ends before calling it: the flag exists to make someone look, and clearing it is the assertion that they did. Idempotent — confirming a link that is not suspect changes nothing. list_links_for_artifact reports `suspect` per link, which is how you find the ones waiting. Proposal-mode agent runs are refused (403) rather than diverted to a proposal: this is a human sign-off, and routing it through a proposal would defeat the review the flag is there to trigger.

tools.name: list_links_for_artifact
tools.description: List all links touching one artifact.

tools.name: add_comment
tools.description: Add a chatter comment to an artifact.

tools.name: list_baselines
tools.description: List a project's baselines.

tools.name: get_baseline
tools.description: Get a baseline's details by ID (name and capture time). The snapshot itself is not returned — read a baseline's content with get_project_map, passing baseline_id.

tools.name: create_baseline
tools.description: Capture a baseline: an immutable snapshot of the project's artifacts and links. Capture one after a coherent set of changes has landed, so later work can be compared against it.

name.description: Optional baseline name (the server names a dated one when omitted)

tools.name: start_project_review
tools.description: Start a review round for a whole project: every artifact still in draft moves to in_review in one action. Re-runnable and safe to repeat — an approved artifact nobody has changed stays approved, while one whose content was edited since it was approved is already back in draft and so is pulled into review again. Covers every artifact type by default, headings and descriptions included; pass types to narrow it.

types.description: Optional artifact types to review (default: every type in the catalog)

tools.name: create_test_run
tools.description: Create a test run in a project.

tools.name: record_test_result
tools.description: Record one test case result in a test run.

tools.name: close_test_run
tools.description: Close a test run once its results are recorded: status "completed", or "aborted" for a run that was abandoned. Only an in-progress run can be closed.

tools.name: get_quality_rules
tools.description: The requirement quality rules this project is judged against: its normative convention ("shall" or RFC 2119 must/should/may) and the severity of each lint rule, plus a one-sentence summary. Read this before drafting or rewording a requirement so the wording matches the project's house style.

tools.name: get_quality_findings
tools.description: Lint one requirement or user need against the project's quality rules: a 0-100 score, its band, and one finding per wording problem (weak words, vague quantifiers, placeholders, passive voice, off-convention keywords, over-long sentences, untestable phrasing). Advisory — findings never block a write.

artifact_id.description: Artifact ID or stable ref (pass project_id to resolve a ref)

project_id.description: Project ID, required when artifact_id is a stable ref

tools.name: get_vv_coverage
tools.description: Verification coverage for a project: the rollup summary plus one line per requirement (verification method, status, rollup). Pass detail=true for the full report, which also carries each requirement's test cases and their latest results.

detail.description: Return the full report instead of the per-requirement summary lines

tools.name: get_vv_gaps
tools.description: Traceability and verification gaps in a project: requirements with no verification method, with no test case, unverified (requirements_unverified — method demonstration, analysis or inspection and not yet marked verified), or whose latest results fail, plus orphan test cases, user needs no requirement derives from, and unmitigated hazards. Each is a list of artifact IDs.

tools.name: list_releases
tools.description: A project's target releases (such as MVP, V1.0) in order, each with its id, name, target date and status (planned, in_progress or released). A requirement introduced in a release is in every later one, until the last release it targets, if it has one.

tools.name: create_release
tools.description: Add a target release to the end of a project's release order.

name.description: Release name, unique in the project (for example MVP or V1.0)

tools.name: update_release
tools.description: Change a target release: its name, description, target date (an empty string clears it) or status. Omitted fields are kept.

target_date.description: New planned date, YYYY-MM-DD, or an empty string to clear it

tools.name: get_release_progress
tools.description: Progress against target releases. Without release_id: every release's counts (requirements in it, introduced in it, approved, verified, ready, and by V&V rollup) and the requirements no release targets. With release_id: that release's counts plus one line per requirement (ref, title, review status, rollup, release range); pass detail=true to add each requirement's test cases and latest results and the day-by-day burn-up.

detail.description: With release_id: return the full progress, test results and burn-up included

release_id.description: Release ID; omit for the overview of every release

tools.name: set_release_target
tools.description: Set the target releases of an artifact: the release it is introduced in (release) and, optionally, the last release it is in (until); it is in every release between them, or every later one when until is empty. Releases are named by id or name. clear=true removes the artifact's own targeting, so it inherits its parent's again. The artifact's other attributes are kept.

clear.description: Remove the artifact's own targeting instead

release.description: First release, by id or name

until.description: Optional last release, by id or name

tools.name: list_work_items
tools.description: List a project's kanban board cards sorted by column and position (no descriptions or activity — use get_work_item for a card's detail). Optionally filter by board column and/or assignee ID.

assignee_id.description: Optional assignee ID filter (agent, user or team ID)

column.description: Optional board column filter: backlog, todo, in-progress, review or done

tools.name: get_work_item
tools.description: Get a kanban work item with its activity.

tools.name: get_work_item_history
tools.description: Get just the activity history of a work item.

tools.name: update_work_item
tools.description: Add a progress comment to a work item.

tools.name: record_candidate_need
tools.description: Record a candidate user need discovered during an interview. Stored as a draft user-need artifact for later review.

need.description: Short statement of the user need

quote.description: Optional supporting quote from the interviewee

requests: POST /api/v1/artifacts {"body":"Rationale: Downtime\n\nQuote: \"We only find out when it leaks.\"","project_id":"11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111","title":"Operators see seal wear early","type":"user-need"}

tools.name: list_todos
tools.description: List a project's to-dos: one-paragraph jobs to tick off, separate from the kanban board. Open ones come first, soonest due first, then the done ones. Set include_done to false to leave the done ones out.

include_done.description: Include to-dos already ticked off (default true)

tools.name: create_todo
tools.description: Add a to-do to a project: one paragraph of text, at most 1000 characters, for a small job someone just does and ticks off. Optionally assign it to a project member and give it a due date (YYYY-MM-DD). Larger work with discussion belongs on the board as a work item.

assignee_id.description: Optional user ID of the project member who has it

tools.name: tick_todo
tools.description: Tick a to-do off as done, or set done to false to open it again.

done.description: true to tick it off (the default), false to open it again

tools.name: get_plan
tools.description: Read a project's plan: every board task in outline order with its start and due dates, parent task, progress (from its to-dos and sub-tasks), its duration and float in working days, its effort in days, whether it is on the critical path (the chain of tasks that decides the plan's end, which may still have float) and the day its end can slip to before it pushes the next task, its relationships to the tasks that drive it (FS, SS or FF) and whether it is late; the milestones in date order, each target release among them, with their completion criteria measured against the project's artifacts; and every metric a criterion can name with its current value.

tools.name: schedule_work_item
tools.description: Place a board task on the plan: its start date and due date (YYYY-MM-DD), its duration in working days and effort in days (a task with sub-tasks takes all four from them and refuses them), its parent task (making it a sub-task) and its relationships to the tasks that drive it. A relationship is written "<work item id>:<type>", where the type is FS (finish to start: this task starts after that one finishes), SS (start to start: it starts no earlier than that one starts) or FF (finish to finish: it finishes no earlier than that one finishes); with no type it is FS. A task may have several, so two tasks can together drive when it starts. Only the arguments you pass change; pass an empty string to clear a date or the parent, and an empty relationships list to clear them. Answers the task's row of the plan.

actual_cost.description: What the task has really cost so far; "-1" goes back to its earned share of the planned cost

actual_finish.description: The day work really finished, YYYY-MM-DD; an empty string clears it

actual_start.description: The day work really started, YYYY-MM-DD; an empty string clears it

after_id.description: Work item ID of the sibling task this one goes straight after in the outline; an empty string makes it the first of its siblings. Siblings are otherwise listed by start date

assignments.description: Who the task is assigned to on the plan, each "user:<id>" or "agent:<id>", with an optional share of their time after it as in "user:<id>:50" (percent; 100 when left out); replaces the task's assignments, and an empty list leaves it to the board's assignee

constraint_type.description: A date constraint: "asap" (none), "alap" (as late as possible), "snet"/"snlt" (start no earlier/later than), "fnet"/"fnlt" (finish no earlier/later than), "mso"/"mfo" (must start/finish on). Every one but asap and alap needs constraint_date

deadline.description: The day the task should be finished by, YYYY-MM-DD; it moves nothing, and the plan flags a task that misses it. An empty string clears it

depends_on.description: Earlier form of relationships: work item IDs, each finish to start unless it already has a type

due_date.description: Due date, YYYY-MM-DD; an empty string clears it

duration_days.description: How long the task runs, in whole working days counting its first and last; the task keeps it, so a start date sent alone moves the due date and a due date sent alone moves the start. "0" clears it

effort_days.description: The work in the task, in person-days (may be a decimal); "0" clears it

effort_driven.description: "true" lets the task's effort and the people on it decide its duration

elapsed.description: "true" makes the duration count calendar days, weekends and holidays included (a cure, a delivery); "false" counts working days

fixed_cost.description: What the task costs beyond the time of the people on it; "0" clears it

milestone.description: Key of the milestone the task is assigned to, as get_plan lists it (a milestone's id, or "release:<release id>"); an empty string takes it off. The milestone then counts the task among its tasks done

mode.description: The task's own scheduling mode: "manual" (it stays where it is put), "auto" (the platform places it from its relationships and constraint), or an empty string to take the plan's

parent_id.description: Work item ID of the parent task; an empty string makes it a top-level task

percent_complete.description: How complete the task is, "0" to "100", in place of the progress counted from its to-dos and sub-tasks; "-1" goes back to the counted progress

relationships.description: The tasks that drive this one, each "<work item id>:FS", ":SS", ":FF" or ":SF", with an optional offset after it as in "<id>:SS:5" (working days; negative leads), "<id>:FS:3ed" (elapsed days) or "<id>:SS:50%" (of the driving task's duration); replaces the task's relationships

start_date.description: Start date, YYYY-MM-DD; an empty string clears it

tools.name: recalculate_plan
tools.description: Recalculate a project's plan: move each task that another task drives, or that a constraint holds to a date, to the dates those ask for. A task keeps its duration; a task nothing places, and a task that is done, stay where they are. Answers how many tasks moved. A manual plan's tasks move only on this call; an automatic plan's are placed after every change.

only_later.description: "true" treats relationships as minimums: a task already on or after the day asked is left where it is

tools.name: set_plan_calendar
tools.description: Set a project's plan holidays, its critical threshold and how it is scheduled. holidays replaces the plan's days off (days it does not work whatever the weekday), each "YYYY-MM-DD" or "YYYY-MM-DD:Name"; critical_slack_days is the float, in working days, at or below which a task counts as critical ("0" by default); scheduling_mode "auto" has the platform place every task from its relationships and constraints after each change, "manual" (the default) leaves tasks where they are put. An argument left out stays as it is. Answers every setting as stored.

active_baseline_id.description: ID of the baseline variance and earned value are measured against, as get_plan lists under baselines; an empty string means the newest

budget.description: What the plan may cost; "0" clears it

critical_slack_days.description: Float in working days at or below which a task is critical, "0" to "365"

currency.description: The money costs are in, as up to three letters, e.g. "GBP"

holidays.description: The plan's holidays, each "YYYY-MM-DD" or "YYYY-MM-DD:Name"; an empty list clears them

multiple_critical_paths.description: "true" gives each chain of tasks a critical path of its own, to its own last task

project_finish.description: The day the plan must finish by, YYYY-MM-DD: float is counted to it. An empty string clears it

project_start.description: The day the plan starts, YYYY-MM-DD: an automatic task starts no earlier. An empty string clears it

schedule_from.description: "start" (tasks as soon as possible) or "finish" (automatic tasks as late as possible)

scheduling_mode.description: "manual" or "auto": the mode of every task that has none of its own

status_date.description: The day progress is reported as of, YYYY-MM-DD: earned value and behind-schedule marks are measured at it. An empty string means today

tools.name: set_plan_resource
tools.description: Set what a day of a person's or an agent's time costs on a project, and the share of a working day they can give it. The plan costs each task from its people's rates, and reports anyone asked for more than their capacity. get_plan lists who can be assigned under people.

capacity.description: The percentage of a working day they can give the project; "100" when left out

daily_rate.description: What a day of their time costs, in the plan's currency

id.description: The user's or the agent's ID

tools.name: level_plan
tools.description: Level a project's plan: delay tasks until no person or agent is asked for more than their capacity on any day. Where someone is over-allocated the task with the most float is delayed until after the first of the others ends, and the tasks it drives follow. Answers how many tasks moved.

tools.name: set_plan_working_days
tools.description: Set which days of the week a project's plan works, as ISO weekday numbers from "1" (Monday) to "7" (Sunday). A task's duration and float count only working days, so a plan that works Monday to Friday (the default) leaves weekends out. Answers the working days as stored.

working_days.description: ISO weekday numbers, "1" (Monday) to "7" (Sunday); at least one

tools.name: save_plan_baseline
tools.description: Save a baseline of a project's plan: every task's dates, duration, effort and cost as they stand, kept so get_plan can report how far each task has moved since (its variance) and the plan's earned value. A plan keeps at most 11. Answers the baseline's id and name.

name.description: What to call it; "Baseline <today>" when left out

tools.name: reschedule_remaining_work
tools.description: Move the work that should have started by the plan's status date and has not to that date, and the tasks it drives after it. A task with progress or an actual start, and a task that is done, stay where they are. Answers how many tasks moved.
